name: District of Columbia

agency.name: Office of Workers' Compensation, Department of Employment Services (DOES)

ttd.rateText: 66 2/3% of the employee's average weekly wages during the continuance of temporary total disability (D.C. Code § 32-1508(2)).
ttd.minText: DOES minimum compensation rate for 2026 (D.C. Code § 32-1505).

waiting.text: No compensation is allowed for the first 3 days of disability, except medical benefits under § 32-1507; if the injury results in disability of more than 14 days, compensation is allowed from the date of disability (D.C. Code § 32-1505).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid during the continuance of total disability, with no fixed week cap; temporary partial disability is limited to 5 years (D.C. Code § 32-1508(2), (5)).

ppd.text: Scheduled permanent partial disability pays 66 2/3% of average weekly wages for a fixed number of weeks (e.g. arm 312 weeks, leg 288, hand 244), proportionally for partial loss of use (D.C. Code § 32-1508(3)).

statute.cite: D.C. Code §§ 32-1505, 32-1508 (District of Columbia Workers' Compensation Act of 1979)

facts.text: DC's 2026 weekly maximum is $1,852.07, up 2.40% from $1,808.66 in 2025; the DOES table goes back to $396.78 in 1982.
The DOES minimum rate is set at one-quarter of the maximum ($463.02 vs. $1,852.07 in 2026), as in every year of its table since 1982.
Annual supplemental allowances (cost-of-living increases) for long-term disability recipients are capped at 5% (D.C. Code § 32-1506(d)).
Temporary partial disability benefits (66 2/3% of wage loss) cannot be paid for more than 5 years (D.C. Code § 32-1508(5)).

uncertain: The exact statutory minimum rule (and whether workers earning less than the minimum receive their actual wage) was not read; minText cites only the DOES table.
